Articles.title: Correspondence address and domicile in Geneva: what your declaration commits you to
Articles.description: Telling apart three often-confused notions in Geneva: civil domicile, tax domicile as the centre of vital interests, and notification to the residents' register — and what an inaccurate declaration can trigger.
Articles.content:
We commonly speak of an "address" as if it were a single thing. In reality, that word hides several distinct legal notions, which do not obey the same rules and do not carry the same consequences. Confusing the address where you receive your mail with domicile in the legal sense is a common mistake — and sometimes a costly one. Here is how to untangle these notions in Geneva, with the official sources for each point. We quote here neither an article nor a precise penalty: the linked text prevails and evolves.

## Three notions not to confuse

The first step is to name what we are talking about. A correspondence address is simply the place where you choose to receive your mail: it is practical, revocable, and does not, on its own, establish your domicile. Domicile, on the other hand, is a legal notion, and it actually comes in several forms depending on the context. Failing to distinguish these planes leads to the belief that a mere postal address would suffice to fix one's situation — which it does not.

## Civil domicile: where the centre of your life is

Under the Civil Code, a person's domicile is the place where they reside with the intention of settling there. It is not a formal declaration that creates it, but a reality: effective presence coupled with the will to make this place one's centre. Civil domicile carries many effects — legal forum, civil status, the exercise of certain rights. The framework can be consulted in the [Swiss Civil Code (CC)](https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/24/233_245_233/fr). The key point: civil domicile is established by fact, it is not decreed at will through a chosen address.

## Tax domicile: the centre of vital interests

In tax matters, the notion is neighbouring but not identical. Tax domicile attaches to the centre of vital interests: the place where your personal and economic ties concentrate — family, effective housing, social and professional life. It is this centre, not the declared address, that determines where you are taxed. A person can therefore be tax-domiciled where their life actually takes place, even if their mail arrives elsewhere. The principles appear in the [DFTA](https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1991/1184_1184_1184/fr) and the [THA](https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1991/1256_1256_1256/fr). Here too, it is substance that counts, not the label.

## Notification to the residents' register

The third notion is administrative. Anyone who settles in the canton must register with the OCPM, which fulfils the role of residents' register in Geneva, and report their changes. This notification feeds the official registers and is a precondition for a great many procedures. It is not optional, and it must reflect reality: you declare the place where you actually live, not an address of convenience. The procedure and the competent counters appear on the canton's pages, in particular via the [Cantonal Population and Migration Office (OCPM)](https://www.ge.ch/organisation/office-cantonal-population-migrations-ocpm).

## What an inaccurate declaration can trigger

This is where carelessness becomes risk. Declaring a domicile that does not match reality — for instance to benefit from a more favourable regime, or through mere negligence — is not trivial. An inaccurate declaration can constitute an offence and expose you, on the tax side, to a reassessment: the authority can restore the real situation and revise your taxation accordingly. We quote here neither an article nor a penalty amount: these elements belong to the official texts and their application, which you must check with the canton. The principle to retain is simple: the declaration must reflect the facts, and the facts prevail over the displayed address.

## The useful habit: aligning the declared with the real

Safety rests on one thing: that what you declare — mail, residents' register, tax situation — is consistent with where your life actually takes place. Tensions always arise from the gap: an address in one canton, a life in another; a declared domicile that does not withstand scrutiny. For an international household, whose ties are sometimes spread across several countries, this work of coherence deserves to be done calmly, once, rather than endured later.

## Our role: to clarify, not to circumvent

Ridger does not offer a correspondence address or domiciliation to individuals, and proposes no arrangement designed to make a domicile appear that would not correspond to the reality of your life. Our contribution is one of clarity: we help you understand which of these notions applies to your situation, bring your declarations into coherence, and document the facts that ground your real domicile. When the question becomes legal or contentious, we liaise with your lawyer or tax specialist. It is the discipline of a family office: bringing order where approximation is expensive. [Let's clarify your situation](/en/services/tax-administration/).

The notions and consequences mentioned belong to regularly amended texts: the linked official page prevails, and we verified them on 2026-09-20.

Articles.title: The essential insurance policies of a Geneva household
Articles.description: What a household must cover when settling in Geneva: compulsory health insurance and its deadline, private liability and household insurance — and why Ridger coordinates without being an intermediary.
Articles.content:
Arriving in Geneva also means entering an insurance system unlike that of any other country. Some cover is compulsory and subject to strict deadlines; other cover is optional but expected, notably by letting agencies. Finding your bearings early avoids two symmetrical pitfalls: the coverage gap that proves expensive, and the over-insurance that needlessly ties up budget. Here is an overview of the policies that structure a household's life, with the official sources. We quote no premium here: the amounts belong to the insurers and the official pages, and vary widely.

## Health insurance: compulsory, and quickly

The centrepiece is compulsory health care insurance, within the meaning of the Health Insurance Act (LAMal). It is not a choice: anyone settling in Switzerland must take it out. The point new arrivals underestimate is the deadline. Affiliation must occur within three months of taking up residence; if you meet this deadline, cover is retroactive to the date of arrival, so no period is left uncovered. Conversely, affiliating beyond that deadline forfeits this retroactivity and may entail a premium surcharge. In other words: the clock starts ticking the moment you settle in. The framework can be consulted on [bag.admin.ch — Compulsory health care insurance](https://www.bag.admin.ch/bag/fr/home/versicherungen/krankenversicherung.html) and, for premiums, on [priminfo.admin.ch](https://www.priminfo.admin.ch/fr).

## Choosing your fund and model

Basic insurance is standardised in its content — the benefits covered are defined by law and identical from one insurer to another — but the premiums differ, as do the models (free choice of doctor, family doctor, care network) and the amount of the deductible you retain. This is where most of the budgetary trade-off is decided. The official comparator [priminfo.admin.ch](https://www.priminfo.admin.ch/fr) lets you objectify this choice for your canton and municipality. We recommend neither a fund nor a model here: the decision depends on your situation and your relationship to risk.

## Exemptions and special cases

The principle of compulsory affiliation has exceptions. Certain people may, under precise conditions, be exempted from Swiss insurance — for instance certain G-permit holders who remain covered in their State of residence, or other cross-border situations. These exemptions are neither automatic nor general: they are obtained on request, within deadlines, and according to criteria that only the authority validates. The [ge.ch — Health insurance](https://www.ge.ch/dossier/assurance-maladie) page sets out the cases and the procedure in the canton. The prudent habit is to check your situation before the deadline, not after.

## Private liability insurance

Beyond health, one cover is imposed in practice: private liability insurance. It is not compulsory in the legal sense for a household in general (exceptions exist, notably for dog owners), but it answers for the damage you, your family or your animals might cause to third parties — and those amounts can be high. Most letting agencies in fact require it when signing a lease. Treating it as optional amounts to betting against an asymmetric risk: low cost, potentially heavy exposure.

## Household insurance

Its cousin is household insurance, which covers your movable property against theft, fire, water damage and other losses. Also optional in the eyes of the law, it is frequently expected by the landlord and, above all, it protects a domestic estate whose replacement value is often underestimated. It is commonly taken out together with liability cover in a single contract. Here again, the point is not to cover everything, but to cover exactly right.

## Household insurance and the lease

One practical detail deserves attention: many Geneva letting agencies ask, when handing over the keys, for a private liability insurance certificate, sometimes coupled with household insurance. Anticipating this document avoids a last-minute blockage when moving in. It is best to have the certificate ready before the date of entry into the accommodation, and to keep it with the lease file.

## A clear order of priorities

For a household settling in, the order is simple: first sort out health insurance, under time pressure, then liability and household insurance, often required at the time of the lease, and finally supplementary cover according to your real needs. This hierarchy avoids chasing a late affiliation while paying for accessory options. It is a sequencing, as much as a list.

## Our role: to coordinate, without being an intermediary

A point of clarity is needed. Ridger is not an insurance intermediary: insurance intermediation is a regulated activity, falling under FINMA and the Insurance Supervision Act (LSA), and we do not advise on the choice of a product, an insurer or a premium, nor do we receive any commission from an insurer. Our contribution is organisational: we help you identify the cover that concerns you, meet the deadlines — first and foremost the LAMal deadline — and gather the documents at the right moment, liaising where necessary with your broker or insurer. It is the logic of a family office: bringing order to the administrative foundations of your move, without encroaching on regulated professions. [Let's coordinate your move](/en/services/family-office-coordination/).

The deadlines, exemptions and premiums mentioned belong to regularly amended texts and tariffs: the linked official page prevails, and we verified them on 2026-09-20.

Articles.title: Exchanging your foreign driving licence in Geneva
Articles.description: The procedure for exchanging a foreign driving licence at the Cantonal Vehicle Office in Geneva: the deadline for new residents, the cases where a test is required, and Ridger's coordination role.
Articles.content:
Driving in Geneva with a licence obtained abroad follows a rule that is simple in principle, but comes with a deadline you must not miss. Many new residents believe their original licence remains valid indefinitely; it does not. After a certain time, exchanging it for a Swiss licence becomes compulsory, and neglecting it amounts to driving without a valid licence. Here is how to approach this step in Geneva, with the official sources. We quote here neither a list of countries nor a deadline figure from memory: these elements appear on the linked cantonal page and evolve.

## The principle: a foreign licence only lasts so long

On arrival, your foreign driving licence allows you to drive for a limited period. Beyond that, the rule requires you to exchange it for a Swiss licence; it is an obligation, not a mere option. The count of this deadline starts from when you take up residence, which makes it one of the steps to schedule early in your arrival calendar. The general principle can be consulted on [ch.ch — Driving in Switzerland with a foreign licence](https://www.ch.ch/fr/vehicules-et-circulation/permis-de-conduire/permis-de-conduire-etranger/).

## The competent authority: the Cantonal Vehicle Office

In Geneva, the step is carried out with the Cantonal Vehicle Office (OCV). It receives the application, checks the documents, and issues the Swiss licence in exchange for the foreign one. The procedure generally requires assembling a file — identity document, original licence, photo, eyesight certificate, and in some cases other documents — and following the arrangements specific to the canton. The pages [ge.ch — Cantonal Vehicle Office (OCV)](https://www.ge.ch/organisation/office-cantonal-vehicules-ocv) and [ge.ch — Exchanging a foreign driving licence](https://www.ge.ch/echanger-permis-conduire-etranger) set out the procedure, the forms and the counters.

## The new residents' deadline

The most sensitive point is the deadline. The rule provides that the exchange take place within a set period after taking up residence; beyond that, not only is the exchange still due, but your foreign licence ceases to allow you to drive, and a test may then become necessary. This is precisely the trap: believing you have all the time in the world and letting the deadline pass. Rather than relying on a figure heard elsewhere, check the exact deadline in force on the [ge.ch — Exchanging a foreign driving licence](https://www.ge.ch/echanger-permis-conduire-etranger) page, and start the step without waiting for the final weeks.

## With or without a test: it depends on the country of origin

Not all exchanges are alike. Depending on the State that issued your licence, the exchange may be direct, or subject to a test — theory, practical, or both. The distinction rests on official lists of States whose licences are recognised without a driving check, lists that only the official page establishes. We reproduce none of these lists here: they are liable to change, and outdated information could mislead you. Good practice is to identify, from the outset, which case applies to you, so as to plan, where relevant, the time and preparation for a test.

## Driving while the exchange is pending

A question comes up often: can you keep driving while the exchange is being processed? As long as the deadline has not expired and your foreign licence remains valid, you drive normally in principle. The care to take is not to confuse the validity of your original licence with the cantonal exchange deadline: these are two distinct clocks, and it is the second that triggers the obligation. Keeping your original licence on you and, once the application is filed, the receipts issued by the office, remains a simple precaution.

## Anticipating: a step with knock-on effects

Exchanging the licence is not just an isolated formality. It conditions your ability to drive day to day, to rent or register a vehicle, sometimes to organise family life in a region where the car remains useful. Handling it early, alongside the other arrival steps, avoids discovering too late that you are no longer entitled to take the wheel. It is precisely the kind of point that, sorted in time, goes unnoticed — and, forgotten, is paid for in hassle.

## Our role: coordinating the step

Ridger does not issue licences and does not replace the Cantonal Vehicle Office: the decision belongs to the authority. Our contribution is coordination. We help you situate your case — direct exchange or test —, gather the documents in the right order, meet the deadline that runs from when you settle in, and fit this step into the overall calendar of your arrival, alongside the other formalities. It is the logic of a family office: a single point of contact ensuring no deadline slips by unnoticed. [Let's coordinate your arrival steps](/en/services/family-office-coordination/).

The deadline, documents and lists of States mentioned are set by the authorities and amended regularly: the linked official page prevails, and we verified them on 2026-09-20.
